enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 124 of 2018, under Sections 354D, 306 and
506 I.P.C., Police Station-Meja, District-Allahabad, during the pendency of the trial. 4. It transpires from the record that on the fateful day, i.e. on 14.03.2018, a young
girl, namely, Kanchan Devi committed suicide by immolating herself. The first
information report in respect of the aforesaid incident was lodged on 14.03.2018 by
the mother of the deceased, which came to be registered as Case Crime No. 0124 of
2018, under Sections 354D, 306, 511 and 506 I.P.C., Police Station-Meja,
District-Allahabad. 5. In the aforesaid F.I.R., two persons, namely, Ajay Kumar and Anjana (the
applicant herein) were nominated as named accused. It is the case of the prosecution
that after the happening of the occurrence on 14.03.2018, the victim was admitted to
S.R.N. Hospital, Allahabad where she had undergone treatment upto 25.03.2018. Ultimately, the victim died on 25.03.2018. While the victim was undergoing
treatment at the aforesaid Hospital her dying declaration was recorded on
15.03.2018. The allegations in the F.I.R. clearly implicated the present applicant on
account of eve teasing and molestation. The prosecution version as unfolded in the
F.I.R. also stands corroborated by the dying declaration of the deceased which is on
the record at page 16 of the paper-book as Annexure-3 to the affidavit. Learned
inasmuch as the applicant is the resident of the same village where the victim
/deceased was residing. 6. Be that as it may, there is nothing on the record to disbelieve the dying declaration
of the deceased upto this stage.

record. He therefore submits that the applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail. Therefore, interest of justice shall better be served in
case a direction is issued to the trial court to expedite the trial itself instead of
considering the bail application of the applicant on merits. On the aforesaid factual
premise, he submits that the applicant is not entitled to any indulgence by this Court. The bail application of the applicant is thus liable to be rejected. However, at this stage, it is expected from the learned trial court to gear up the
trial and make necessary endeavour to conclude the same within six months provided
the applicant would render all necessary co-operation in early conclusion of the trial. Office is directed to communicate the copy of this order forthwith to concerned
court for necessary compliance. "
